title: SLA policing, traffic-slices, and tenant ejection experiment notes
content:
Summary:

This working doc captures a proposed, experiment-driven approach to enforcing contract SLAs and preventing noisy-tenant interference across regions. The goal: translate high-level contracted SLAs (tail latency targets, throughput guarantees, availability %) into a set of actionable, measurable runtime controls that live in the control plane and are applied by the data plane routing layer.

Key ideas and constraints (short):
- Decouple decision logic (control plane) from fast path routing (data plane). Control plane issues compact per-tenant policies and short-lived tokens; data plane enforces them with minimal per-request computation.
- Use traffic-slices (time-windowed allocation slices) to reserve a percentage of capacity for SLAed tenants while leaving opportunistic capacity for best-effort tenants.
- Provide both soft backpressure (latency-aware request shaping) and hard ejection (temporary eviction to lower-tier routing) with observable counters and telemetry.
- Multi-region: enabled with cross-region capacity mapping + regional fallback pairs. Avoid split-brain by preferring deterministic per-org region affinity derived from contract metadata and regional health signals.

Signals used for decisions:
- Per-tenant token consumption (tokens per second, tokens per minute) + rolling percentiles of per-call latency (p50/p95/p99)
- Queue depth and GPU utilization on serving nodes (region-level aggregates)
- Model-level sequence length distribution and KV cache hit rates (because these affect per-token cost)
- Recent error spike / 5xx rates per tenant and per-region
- Contract metadata: committed throughput, committed latency SLO, priority tier, geographic constraints, fallback region list

Policy translation (high-level -> runtime knobs):
1) SLA translation: committed throughput -> guaranteed token slice per minute; latency SLO -> max allowed queue latency and dynamic priority weight; availability SLA -> minimum reachable regional capacity margin.
2) Pricing-derived throttling: where tenants exceed soft burst budget, optionally apply token-based charge and reduce priority weight.
3) Noisy neighbor mitigation: detect tenants with sharp deviation in per-token cost (e.g., long sequence lengths or many cache-miss sessions) and apply temporary per-tenant multiplier on token budget.

Traffic-slice model (experiment alpha):
- Each region divides capacity into N slices per epoch (epoch=10s). Slices: guaranteed (for SLAed tenants), reserved-burst (allocated but chargeable), best-effort pool (shared).
- A tenant with committed throughput X gets assigned G guaranteed slices proportional to X / region_capacity. Guaranteed slices are served ahead of best-effort but can be throttled if latency targets are violated.
- The runtime implements a circular allocation: on each epoch, data plane consumes from tenant slice queues in round-robin order with priority weights.

Ejection and fallback modes:
Soft-ejection:
- Trigger: tenant p95 latency > SLA_threshold * 1.25 OR region queue depth above regional_shed_threshold
- Action: move tenant to soft-ejected state for T_soft (default 30s): allowed to consume only from reserved-burst at reduced weight; return to normal if metrics recover for M_recovery window.
Hard-ejection:
- Trigger: sustained errors > 10% or tenant causing > 20% capacity variance for 60s
- Action: route all traffic for tenant to fallback model variants / cheaper quantized variants or to dedicated degraded path (higher latency, lower cost). Notify control plane; create incident if contracted SLA affected.
Graceful regional cutover:
- When a region is unhealthy, control plane uses deterministic fallback list to migrate tenant slices to next region. Migration uses shadow routing: replicate a configurable fraction of requests to fallback region (shadow) to validate capacity/latency before cutover.

Control plane primitives (compact and serializable):
- per_tenant_slice: tenant_id, epoch_ms, guaranteed_quota, burst_quota, priority_weight, fallback_region, ejection_state, version
- ratelimit_token_spec: token_rate_per_minute, refill_burst, ttl
- eviction_annotation: reason_code, started_at, expected_recovery_ms, origin_controller_id
These primitives must be representable in under ~1KB to keep control-plane heartbeat small when pushing to thousands of tenants.

Data plane enforcement (fast path):
- Use a token-bucket consumer per-tenant in the front proxy; token grants come from a local refill loop that applies per-tenant_slice in memory.
- Keep slice epochs aligned with control plane heartbeats (heartbeat < epoch). If control-plane fails, data-plane falls back to last-known slices with embedded expiry.
- Minimal arbitration: per-request check is (has_token? then accept) else consult local probabilistic admission (10% chance to sample for shadow) to avoid hot-looping control plane.

Simulation and experiment plan (short-term milestones):
- Week 1-2: Build a discrete-event simulator (python) that models tenants with different sequence length distributions, request patterns (poisson vs bursty), and regional capacity. Measure p50/p95/p99 for tenants and global fairness index (Jain).
- Week 3: Run tenant mix scenarios: (a) many small fair tenants; (b) small + 2 noisy tenants with long sequences; (c) sudden 10x spike from medium tenant. Capture percent of tenants missing SLA, average tail latency, and wasted capacity.
- Week 4: Iterate on ejection thresholds, slice counts, and epoch length. Export candidate config sets for canary on staging.
- Canary: Use 5% production traffic with shadow routing to fallback region and stepwise enable ejection actions (soft only, then soft+hard).

Operational checklist for rollout (engineering must verify):
- Telemetry: per-tenant p50/p95/p99, per-region queue depth, per-model kv-cache hit rate, per-tenant error-rate. Dashboards and alerts pre-created.
- Audit trail: every ejection has an audit event with origin controller id + reason_code persisted to control plane logs.
- Circuit breakers: global capacity circuit-breaker that flips to degrade non-SLAed tenants when global_util > 85% for 30s.
- Incident playbook: owner assigned, rollback path documented (disable ejections via control-plane flag), and customer communication templates prepared for potential false positives.

Sample policy pseudocode (simplified):

on_heartbeat("tenant_slice_update"):
    for tenant in updates:
        set local_slice[tenant.id] = updates[tenant.id]

on_request(req):
    slice = local_slice.get(req.tenant)
    if not slice or slice.expired():
        if global_circuit_open(): return reject_fast(req)
        else: slice = last_known_slice(req.tenant)

    if token_bucket.consume(slice):
        proceed(req)
    else:
        if slice.priority_weight >= guaranteed_threshold:
            schedule_retry_with_backoff(req)
        else:
            reject_or_enqueue_best_effort(req)

Risk matrix (short):
- False ejection of enterprise tenant -> customer impact, SLA breach. Mitigation: require two independent signals + increase soft-to-hard transition time by default.
- Control plane lag/partitions -> stale slices cause underutilization. Mitigation: fallback to last-known slices with expiry and increase epoch length for safety.
- Cross-region data transfer / compliance issues on fallback -> ensure per-tenant geofence metadata is enforced before routing to fallback.

Open design questions / TODOs:
- Should priority weight computation incorporate model-adjusted cost (sequence length expectations)? Option A: precomputed expected_cost_multiplier in tenant metadata. Option B: reactively infer cost and adjust multiplier.
- How to surface per-tenant fairness SLAs to commercial teams so they can opt into different fallback policies? We need mapping in billing + contract system.
- Policy discovery API: lightweight gRPC stream vs control-plane push. Which scales better for ~20k tenants? (Perf spec required)

Notes to self / action items:
- Ravi: prototype simulator skeleton and attach to this doc (JIRA-INF-3421).
- Elena: draft control-plane schema PR for per_tenant_slice (github PR link above). Include compact binary encoding + protobuf.
- Noah: add dashboard panels in grafana template showing ejection_count_by_tenant and slice_consumption_heatmap.
- Priya: coordinate legal on cross-region fallback constraints for regulated customers.

References and inspiration:
- Borrowed ideas from multi-tenant queueing literature, Netflix Hystrix-like circuit strategies, and recent research on tail latencies in multi-tenant GPU inference.

Quick TL;DR for execs: implement a slice-based guarantee model where the control plane issues compact per-tenant quotas and ejection states. Run simulator-driven experiments, canary with shadow routing, and adopt conservative thresholds for early rollout. The approach balances predictable guarantees for contracted customers with a pragmatic, observable way to mitigate noisy neighbors without catastrophic global outages.
